**Ray Jackson** (born November 13, 1973)[[1]](Ray_Jackson_(basketball)#cite_note-1) is an American former professional [basketball](Basketball "Basketball") player. He is most well known for his time as a member of the [Fab Five](Fab_Five_(University_of_Michigan) "Fab Five (University of Michigan)") with the [Michigan Wolverines](Michigan_Wolverines_men's_basketball "Michigan Wolverines men's basketball").

## College career

Jackson was part of the famed [University of Michigan](University_of_Michigan "University of Michigan") [Wolverines](Michigan_Wolverines "Michigan Wolverines") [Fab Five](Fab_Five_(University_of_Michigan) "Fab Five (University of Michigan)") along with former NBA players [Chris Webber](Chris_Webber "Chris Webber"), [Jimmy King](Jimmy_King "Jimmy King"), [Jalen Rose](Jalen_Rose "Jalen Rose"), and [Juwan Howard](Juwan_Howard "Juwan Howard") that reached the [1992](1992_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "1992 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament") & [1993](1993_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Tournament "1993 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament") [NCAA](National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association") [Men's Division I Basketball Championship](NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship "NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship") games as both Freshmen and Sophomores.

Although the Fab Five final four appearances have been forfeited,[[2]](Ray_Jackson_(basketball)#cite_note-MB07-8p8-2) he was not among the players called before the [grand jury](Grand_jury "Grand jury") ([Robert Traylor](Robert_Traylor "Robert Traylor"), Webber, Rose, [Maurice Taylor](Maurice_Taylor "Maurice Taylor") and [Louis Bullock](Louis_Bullock "Louis Bullock"))[[3]](Ray_Jackson_(basketball)#cite_note-FUaatiMc-3) in the [University of Michigan basketball scandal](University_of_Michigan_basketball_scandal "University of Michigan basketball scandal") and was not found to have received large amounts of money.[[4]](Ray_Jackson_(basketball)#cite_note-4)

Jackson and King were the only two members of the Fab Five to stay at Michigan for their full four years of eligibility; Webber left after his sophomore year and Rose and Howard after their junior years. Jackson's best season at Michigan came in his senior year, as he averaged a team-high of nearly 16 points per game.

## Professional career

Known for his time as one member of the Fab Five, Jackson was not drafted by an [NBA](National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") team and never played in the league. He was cut in preseason by the [New York Knicks](New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") before the 1995–96 season and cut by the [Detroit Pistons](Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") before the 1996–97 season. He was drafted in the [Continental Basketball Association](Continental_Basketball_Association "Continental Basketball Association") (CBA) by the [Grand Rapids Hoops](Grand_Rapids_Hoops "Grand Rapids Hoops") #35 in the 3rd round in 1995.
